current.text: He is the projected starting center in a lineup of Haliburton, Nembhard, Nesmith, Siakam and Zubac.
Jay Huff is the backup center. The depth behind Huff is weak (Larry Nance Jr. or Kobe Brown).
His minutes are the main concern. Carlisle keeps center minutes down and Huff is a capable backup, so the experts expect about 30 minutes, not more.
Experts disagree on a bounce-back. Some expect him to be much better running pick and roll with Haliburton. Josh doubts he returns to his top 30 form because of the minutes cap.
His fit is a question: he moves from a very slow team into an uptempo system that needs quicker decisions.
He missed time last season with a fractured rib and an ankle injury, and played only six games for Indiana.
The fractured rib from last season is no concern for this season.
Ranked 60 to 75 in category leagues. Yahoo's rank is too aggressive for categories, and his ESPN ADP around 95 is good value.
In an auction, Josh would pay 11 or 12 USD, 14 USD at most. He went for 16 USD in that mock.
He is the best fantasy target on the Pacers, depending on the platform price.
Indiana is projected to win 46 to 48 games and finish as a top-six seed in the East.
Indiana plays 3, 4 and 3 games in our fantasy playoff weeks, which is not ideal, and has 15 back-to-backs. Carlisle rests players on back-to-backs.

durable.text: An elite rebounder and screener, the best rebounder the Pacers have had since Domantas Sabonis.
A strong post-up player, the best the Pacers have had since Sabonis.
His minutes usually sit around 29 to 30. He played 33 minutes only once, and his production exploded that season.
FG% and rebounds are his big strengths. He clearly lifts a team's FG% on solid volume.
Threes and steals are his weak categories.
His 35th place 9-cat rank in 2024-25 overstated his real value.

note: Zubac gives you elite FG% and rebounds (z +2.6 and +2.5) with no threes and few steals. That makes him a natural fit for punt 3PM and punt STL builds, and his low FT% volume (2.8 attempts) does little damage. Prices range from 5 USD at ESPN to 18 USD at Yahoo, and our league paid 20 USD last season. The experts cap him at about 14 USD and rank him 60 to 75 in categories, so aim for 10 to 14 USD and let someone else pay 20 USD. Early in the season, watch whether Carlisle gives him more than 30 minutes and how the minutes split with Huff. Also note that Indiana plays only 3, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks.
